claim: In Blood the only thing that changes a wall's blocking bits at run time is a kWallGib (type 511) XWALL changing state: SetupGibWallState clears cstat 1|64 on both sides and the masked bit 16 when it turns ON, and when it turns OFF sets 1 on its own side and clears it on the other. A Z-motion sector moves floors and ceilings, never wall cstat, so a blocking two-sided wall that is not a gib wall is shut for ever. The bit is carried per side: a wall pair blocks if EITHER record has it; two sectors are cut apart only if every wall pair between them blocks.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/triggers.cpp:662-689 SetupGibWallState, called only from OperateWall's kWallGib case (:715, :732); no other wall-cstat write in vanilla Blood code clears bit 1 (gameutil.cpp:621-623 in VectorScan clears only 64 and restores it at :640-641; seq.cpp:556-558 clears 8|16|32; mapedit.cpp is the editor).

knowledge/blood/findings/probes/audit2_blocking_walls.py over the 43 campaign maps: 2,272 blocking two-sided wall records, 205 of them kWallGib, all 205 built shut (state 0) and set to break when shot (trigger_vector), 30 also on an rx channel; bloodmap/conditional.py blocking_aware base
use: A breakable wall is a kWallGib XWALL built blocking; a reachability reader ORs both wall records and reopens only what a mechanism drives.

checked.how: Read NBlood/source/blood/src/triggers.cpp:662-689 (SetupGibWallState): state on clears 65 on both sides and 16; state off sets 1 on this side, clears 1 on the other; called only from OperateWall case kWallGib (:715, :732). gameutil.cpp:621-641 (VectorScan) clears 64 and restores it; seq.cpp:556-558 clears 8|16|32 only.
